newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Peres to meet Arafat in Nablus.
newsitem.headline: Peres to meet Arafat in Nablus.

text.p: Israeli opposition leader Shimon Peres will meet Palestinian President Yasser Arafat in the West Bank town of Nablus on Sunday, Israel Radio said on Saturday.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's spokesman Shai Bazak confirmed Netanyahu had approved the meeting.
"The prime minister approved it," Bazak told Reuters.
Peres's spokesman was not immediately available to comment.
The radio did not give a reason for the meeting that Peres, Israel's former prime minister ousted in May elections by less than a percentage point by Netanyahu, would hold with Arafat.
The two last met on August 22.
Peres was a main architect of interim peace deals between Israel and Arafat's Palestine Liberation Organisation that set up Palestinian self-rule in most of the Gaza Strip and parts of the West Bank.

Peres delayed an Israeli troop redeployment in the West Bank town of Hebron that according to a signed accord should have been carried out in March. The delay was decided after Islamic militant suicide bombers killed 59 people in Israel in March and February.
Arabs doubt Netanyahu will honour the deal. Negotiations on implementing it began this week between the sides.

The negotiations were decided on at an emergency Washington summit called in the wake of fierce Palestinian-Israeli clashes last month spurred by Israeli policies in Jerusalem in which 60 Arabs and 15 Jews were killed.
